```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# Locate the project root when running chunks interactively or rendering the post.
here::i_am("blog/posts/2026-09-08-nurburgring-roads-in-r/index.qmd")
source(here::here("blog", "_R", "post_setup.R"))

# Use the same editorial green as the post header.
forest_green <- set_plot_accent_color("#47714D")
install_missing_packages(c("here", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "sf", "osmdata", "tibble", "svglite", "knitr"))

# Keep data and images beside the post, regardless of the working directory.
post_dir <- here::here("blog", "posts", "2026-09-08-nurburgring-roads-in-r")
```

Inspired by
[Bastián Olea's tutorial](https://bastianolea.rbind.io/blog/tutorial_mapas_osm/)
and its [source code](https://github.com/bastianolea/tutorial_r_mapa_openstreetmap/blob/main/tutorial_mapas_osm.qmd).

Let's draw the roads around the Nordschleife, the Eifel's
[**Green Hell**](https://nuerburgring.de/info/nuerburgring/race-tracks/nordschleife):
a soft background, varied line widths and racetracks in green.
Forest green nods to the circuit's nickname, while the grey backgrounds evoke asphalt.

## Map area

Set the screen resolution and map width here. Height follows the screen ratio.
Reduce `width_km` to zoom in; `extra_area_pct` only adds space to the surroundings view.

```{r}
#| label: map-area

screen_width_px <- 2560  # 1440p in landscape orientation.
screen_height_px <- 1440
export_dpi <- 160        # Sets text and stroke scale at the requested pixel dimensions.

centre_lon <- 6.95       # Longitude in decimal degrees, east of Greenwich.
centre_lat <- 50.36      # Latitude in decimal degrees, north of the equator.
width_km <- 16           # Lower this to show less space around the circuit.
extra_area_pct <- 20     # Extra area for the separate surroundings view.

stopifnot(screen_width_px > 0, screen_height_px > 0, export_dpi > 0,
          width_km > 0, extra_area_pct >= 0)

# Match the geographic frame to the screen without stretching the roads.
screen_ratio <- screen_width_px / screen_height_px
height_km <- width_km / screen_ratio

# Use the same proportions for the following figures in the post.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.asp = 1 / screen_ratio)

# Show the projected frame areas before making any download request.
c(detail_km2 = width_km * height_km,
  surroundings_km2 = width_km * height_km * (1 + extra_area_pct / 100))
```

Build both frames in metres using the local UTM projection.

```{r}
#| label: define-map-frames

# EPSG:4326 identifies longitude/latitude coordinates in WGS84.
centre <- sf::st_sfc(sf::st_point(c(centre_lon, centre_lat)), crs = 4326) |>
  sf::st_transform(25832) |>  # ETRS89 / UTM zone 32N uses metres in this region.
  sf::st_coordinates()      # Extract the projected x and y coordinates.

centre <- as.numeric(centre) # Use a plain vector for the frame calculations.

make_frame <- function(width_m, height_m) {
  # Half the width and height on each side keep the rectangle centred.
  sf::st_bbox(c(
    xmin = centre[1] - width_m / 2, ymin = centre[2] - height_m / 2,
    xmax = centre[1] + width_m / 2, ymax = centre[2] + height_m / 2
  ), crs = sf::st_crs(25832)) |>
    sf::st_as_sfc() # Turn the bounds into a polygon for clipping and plotting.
}

width_m <- width_km * 1000   # Convert kilometres to the projection's metre units.
height_m <- height_km * 1000

# Area = width × height: scale both sides by the square root of the area multiplier.
margin_scale <- sqrt(1 + extra_area_pct / 100)

frames <- list(
  circuit = make_frame(width_m, height_m),
  surroundings = make_frame(width_m * margin_scale, height_m * margin_scale)
)

# Reuse these bounds to crop layers and fix the plot limits.
surroundings_bbox <- sf::st_bbox(frames$surroundings)
circuit_bbox <- sf::st_bbox(frames$circuit)
```

## Data

Download once per area and save an RDS. The same settings reuse the file;
changing them creates a separate cache.

```{r}
#| label: load-openstreetmap-data

# Include every area setting so a different frame cannot reuse the wrong data.
area_id <- paste(centre_lon, centre_lat, width_km, height_km, extra_area_pct, sep = "_")

osm_file <- file.path(post_dir, "data", paste0("osm-", area_id, ".rds"))

if (!file.exists(osm_file)) {
  # Overpass needs longitude/latitude bounds; their envelope is slightly larger.
  bbox_wgs84 <- frames$surroundings |> sf::st_transform(4326) |> sf::st_bbox()
  # Ways contain the road and river geometry; timeout is a server time limit in seconds.
  query <- osmdata::opq(bbox = bbox_wgs84, osm_types = "way", timeout = 180) |>
    # The plural function combines filters with OR: highways OR rivers/streams.
    osmdata::add_osm_features(features = c(
      '"highway"', '"waterway"~"^(river|stream)$"' # Match these waterway values exactly.
    ))

  message("Downloading and converting roads and rivers...")
  # Convert the response to sf objects and show progress messages.
  osm <- osmdata::osmdata_sf(query, quiet = FALSE)

  # Place nodes provide label positions without downloading settlement boundaries.
  query_places <- osmdata::opq(bbox = bbox_wgs84, osm_types = "node", timeout = 30) |>
    osmdata::add_osm_feature(key = "place", value = c("town", "village"))

  message("Downloading place names...")
  osm_places <- osmdata::osmdata_sf(query_places, quiet = FALSE)
  # Keep only the two layers used below.
  osm <- list(osm_lines = osm$osm_lines, osm_points = osm_places$osm_points)

  message("Saving data...")
  dir.create(dirname(osm_file), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(osm, osm_file)
}

osm <- readRDS(osm_file)
```

The query uses [`osmdata`](https://docs.ropensci.org/osmdata/articles/osmdata.html).
Separate the roads, waterways and place labels into layers.

```{r}
#| label: prepare-map-layers

roads <- osm$osm_lines |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(highway)) |>       # The highway tag includes paths and racetracks.
  dplyr::select(osm_id, name, highway) |> # Keep useful tags; sf retains the geometry.
  sf::st_transform(25832)

waterways <- osm$osm_lines |>
  dplyr::filter(waterway %in% c("river", "stream")) |>
  sf::st_transform(25832)

# A small selection of place names keeps the map readable.
places <- osm$osm_points |>
  dplyr::filter(place %in% c("town", "village"),
                name %in% c("Nürburg", "Adenau", "Kelberg", "Meuspath")) |>
  sf::st_transform(25832)

# Clip lines to the frame itself: Overpass may return ways that extend outside it.
roads_surroundings <- sf::st_intersection(roads, frames$surroundings)
roads_detail <- sf::st_intersection(roads_surroundings, frames$circuit)

water_detail <- sf::st_crop(waterways, circuit_bbox)

places_detail <- sf::st_crop(places, circuit_bbox)
```

## One line weight

Start with every road drawn alike.

```{r}
#| label: draw-uniform-roads
#| message: false
#| column: page
#| fig-cap: "Every road uses the same colour and line width."
#| fig-alt: "The road network around Nürburgring, drawn in thin grey lines on a light grey background."

library(ggplot2)

asphalt_light <- "#E3E6E4" # A cool, pale grey suggests asphalt without overpowering the lines.
asphalt_dark <- "#303332"  # Charcoal provides the background for the second version.

map_font <- theme_get()$text$family # Reuse the blog's shared typography.

# This map uses a local theme without axes or a grid to keep attention on the roads.
map_theme <- theme_void(base_family = map_font) +
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = asphalt_light, colour = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = asphalt_light, colour = NA),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 7, colour = "#627064", hjust = 0),
    plot.margin = margin(12, 12, 12, 12)
  )

# Fixed limits let us compare styles without changing the close view.
detail_canvas <- ggplot() +
  coord_sf(
    crs = 25832,
    xlim = circuit_bbox[c("xmin", "xmax")], ylim = circuit_bbox[c("ymin", "ymax")],
    expand = FALSE, datum = NA # Add no coordinate padding or latitude/longitude graticule.
  ) +
  labs(caption = "© OpenStreetMap contributors") +
  map_theme

detail_canvas +
  geom_sf(data = roads_detail, colour = "#77817A", linewidth = 0.15)
```

## Line widths

Use `highway` to set a visual hierarchy, including
[`raceway` for racetracks](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Tag:highway%3Draceway).
The widths are design choices, rather than physical road measurements.
Keep every road group, but give minor paths thinner, quieter lines and the
circuit a stronger stroke.

```{r}
#| label: classify-road-hierarchy

# Combine related OSM tags so each road group can share one style.
roads_surroundings <- roads_surroundings |>
  dplyr::mutate(road_group = dplyr::case_when(
    highway == "raceway" ~ "Racetracks",
    highway %in% c("motorway", "motorway_link") ~ "Motorways",
    highway %in% c("trunk", "trunk_link", "primary", "primary_link") ~ "Main roads",
    highway %in% c("secondary", "secondary_link", "tertiary", "tertiary_link") ~ "Regional roads",
    highway %in% c("residential", "living_street", "unclassified") ~ "Local roads",
    highway == "service" ~ "Service roads",
    highway == "track" ~ "Farm and forest tracks",
    highway %in% c("path", "footway", "cycleway", "bridleway", "steps", "pedestrian") ~ "Non-motorised paths",
    TRUE ~ "Other" # Retain tags that do not match one of the groups above.
  ))

# Each group has a colour for light and dark backgrounds; higher draw_order goes on top.
road_style <- tibble::tribble(
  ~road_group, ~line_width, ~line_colour, ~dark_colour, ~draw_order,
  "Other", 0.06, "#D3D8D5", "#3B413E", 0,
  "Non-motorised paths", 0.06, "#CDD3CF", "#3F4742", 1,
  "Farm and forest tracks", 0.08, "#C1CAC4", "#48534B", 2,
  "Service roads", 0.10, "#B8C2BB", "#515E55", 3,
  "Local roads", 0.14, "#A5B2A9", "#606F65", 4,
  "Regional roads", 0.23, "#8C9E91", "#798D80", 5,
  "Main roads", 0.30, "#748B7B", "#90A697", 6,
  "Motorways", 0.38, "#597362", "#A6BAAC", 7,
  "Racetracks", 1.10, forest_green, "#E0EFD9", 8
)

roads_surroundings <- roads_surroundings |>
  dplyr::left_join(road_style, by = "road_group") |> # Attach widths and colours to each road.
  dplyr::arrange(draw_order) # Draw minor paths first and the circuit last.

# Rebuild the close-view layer with its new style columns.
roads_detail <- sf::st_intersection(roads_surroundings, frames$circuit)
```

Keep the colour constant to see what line width changes.

```{r}
#| label: draw-road-width-hierarchy
#| column: page
#| fig-cap: "Line width separates the main roads from minor paths."
#| fig-alt: "The same grey road network, with thicker strokes for racetracks and major roads."

detail_canvas +
  geom_sf(data = roads_detail, aes(linewidth = line_width), colour = "#77817A", lineend = "round") +
  scale_linewidth_identity() # Use the table's widths directly, without rescaling.
```

## Surroundings

Add colour, rivers and place names. The rectangle marks the close view.
Faint grey lines are minor roads and paths, including forest tracks; pale blue
lines are waterways. There are no elevation contours in this map.

```{r}
#| label: draw-surroundings-map
#| column: page
#| fig-cap: "Nürburgring and the surrounding road network."
#| fig-alt: "A wider map with green racetracks, place names and a dashed rectangle marking the close view."

water_colour <- "#C0CECE"

surroundings_map <- ggplot() +
  # Water goes below roads so the circuit remains visible at crossings.
  geom_sf(data = sf::st_crop(waterways, surroundings_bbox), colour = water_colour, linewidth = 0.10) +
  geom_sf(
    data = roads_surroundings, aes(colour = line_colour, linewidth = line_width),
    lineend = "round" # Soften the ends of the individual road segments.
  ) +
  scale_colour_identity() + # Use the hex colours stored in the style table.
  scale_linewidth_identity() +
  # An unfilled rectangle locates the close view without hiding the wider map.
  geom_sf(data = frames$circuit, fill = NA, colour = forest_green, linewidth = 0.25, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_sf_text(
    data = places, aes(label = name), family = map_font, size = 2.5,
    colour = "#34483A", check_overlap = TRUE # Skip labels that overlap earlier labels.
  ) +
  coord_sf(
    crs = 25832,
    xlim = surroundings_bbox[c("xmin", "xmax")], ylim = surroundings_bbox[c("ymin", "ymax")],
    expand = FALSE, datum = NA
  ) +
  labs(caption = "© OpenStreetMap contributors") +
  map_theme

surroundings_map
```

## The circuit in green

Highlight the ways tagged as racetracks. These can include the Nordschleife,
the GP circuit and their connections.

```{r}
#| label: draw-circuit-map
#| column: page
#| fig-cap: "The racetracks stand out within the surrounding roads."
#| fig-alt: "Nürburgring in forest green, surrounded by grey roads on a pale asphalt grey background."

detail_map <- detail_canvas +
  geom_sf(data = water_detail, colour = water_colour, linewidth = 0.10) +
  geom_sf(data = roads_detail, aes(colour = line_colour, linewidth = line_width), lineend = "round") +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  scale_linewidth_identity() +
  geom_sf_text(data = places_detail, aes(label = name), family = map_font, size = 2.5, colour = "#34483A", check_overlap = TRUE)

detail_map
```

## A darker version

The light version uses a soft asphalt grey. Charcoal and lighter roads give
the same map a darker treatment. The preview uses muted forest green (`#47714D`).

```{r}
#| label: draw-dark-circuit-map
#| column: page
#| fig-cap: "The same roads and frame, with colours adjusted for a charcoal background."
#| fig-alt: "Nürburgring in pale green against charcoal, with muted grey-green roads and blue-grey streams."

# Reuse the exact frame and geometries; only the palette changes.
dark_map <- detail_canvas +
  geom_sf(data = water_detail, colour = "#435451", linewidth = 0.10) +
  geom_sf(
    data = roads_detail, aes(colour = dark_colour, linewidth = line_width),
    lineend = "round"
  ) +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  scale_linewidth_identity() +
  geom_sf_text(
    data = places_detail, aes(label = name), family = map_font,
    size = 2.5, colour = "#C0D0C4", check_overlap = TRUE
  ) +
  # Override both backgrounds and the attribution so all remain legible.
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = asphalt_dark, colour = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = asphalt_dark, colour = NA),
    plot.caption = element_text(colour = "#A6B5AB")
  )

dark_map
```

## Save the map

Export both versions as PNG and SVG. The PNGs use the exact screen dimensions
through [`ggsave()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/ggsave.html); SVG stays scalable.

```{r}
#| label: export-road-plate

dir.create(file.path(post_dir, "images"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Pixel dimensions fix the PNG size; dpi controls the physical scale used for styling.
ggsave(file.path(post_dir, "images", "roads-light.png"), detail_map, width = screen_width_px, height = screen_height_px, units = "px", dpi = export_dpi, bg = asphalt_light)
ggsave(file.path(post_dir, "images", "roads-light.svg"), detail_map, width = screen_width_px, height = screen_height_px, units = "px", dpi = export_dpi, bg = asphalt_light)
ggsave(file.path(post_dir, "images", "roads-dark.png"), dark_map, width = screen_width_px, height = screen_height_px, units = "px", dpi = export_dpi, bg = asphalt_dark)
ggsave(file.path(post_dir, "images", "roads-dark.svg"), dark_map, width = screen_width_px, height = screen_height_px, units = "px", dpi = export_dpi, bg = asphalt_dark)
```

```{r}
#| label: generate-roads-preview
#| include: false

# A pale circuit echoes the simple outline against the preview's muted green.
preview_roads <- roads_detail |>
  dplyr::mutate(preview_colour = dplyr::if_else(road_group == "Racetracks", "#EAF1E8", "#56785B"))

preview_map <- ggplot(preview_roads) +
  geom_sf(aes(colour = preview_colour, linewidth = line_width), lineend = "round") +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  scale_linewidth_identity() +
  coord_sf(crs = 25832, xlim = circuit_bbox[c("xmin", "xmax")], ylim = circuit_bbox[c("ymin", "ymax")], expand = FALSE, datum = NA) +
  map_theme +
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = forest_green, colour = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = forest_green, colour = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(8, 8, 8, 8)
  )

ggsave(file.path(post_dir, "images", "preview.png"), preview_map, width = 8, height = 8 / screen_ratio, units = "in", dpi = 150, bg = forest_green)
```
